content: 1. Administer nafcillin at doses of 500 mg IV/IM every 4-6 hours, 1 g IV/IM every 4 hours, or 2 g IV every 4 hours for 4-6 weeks. Treatment duration may be extended, and rifampin and gentamicin may be added if prosthetic materials are present. 2. For suspected penicillin G-resistant streptococcal or staphylococcal infections, initiate therapy with 2 g IV every 4 hours. Severe infections should begin with parenteral therapy, transitioning to oral therapy as clinically indicated. Due to the risk of thrombophlebitis, especially in elderly patients, parenteral administration should be limited to 1-2 days before switching to oral therapy. 3. Nafcillin decreases the levels or effects of cariprazine by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated, as CYP3A4 is responsible for the formation and elimination of cariprazine's active metabolites. The net effect of CYP3A4 inducers on cariprazine exposure is unclear. 4. Nafcillin reduces the levels or effects of cobimetinib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated, as strong or moderate CYP3A4 inducers may decrease cobimetinib systemic exposure by over 80%, reducing its efficacy. 5. Nafcillin decreases the levels or effects of dienogest/estradiol valerate by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. Women should avoid using estradiol valerate/dienogest as contraception while on strong CYP3A4 inducers due to reduced contraceptive efficacy. Estradiol valerate/dienogest should not be used for at least 28 days after discontinuing the inducer. 6. Nafcillin reduces the levels or effects of doravirine by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated, as strong CYP3A4 inducers may decrease doravirine plasma concentrations, leading to loss of virologic response and potential resistance. 7. Nafcillin decreases the levels of elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated, as it may result in loss of virologic response and resistance. 8. Nafcillin reduces the levels or effects of fostemsavir (a prodrug) by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated, as strong CYP3A4 inducers significantly decrease temsavir (the active moiety) plasma concentrations, leading to loss of virologic response and resistance. 9. Nafcillin decreases the levels or effects of isavuconazonium sulfate by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 10. Nafcillin reduces the levels or effects of lonafarnib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated, as lonafarnib is a sensitive CYP3A4 substrate. Avoid co-administration with strong or moderate CYP3A4 inducers. 11. Nafcillin decreases the levels or effects of lorlatinib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. Discontinue the strong CYP3A4 inducer for three plasma half-lives before initiating lorlatinib. 12. Nafcillin reduces the levels or effects of lumacaftor/ivacaftor by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is not recommended, as strong CYP3A4 inducers minimally affect lumacaftor exposure but decrease ivacaftor exposure by 57%, reducing efficacy. 13. Nafcillin decreases the levels or effects of lumefantrine by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated, as it may result in decreased serum concentrations and loss of antimalarial efficacy. 14. Nafcillin reduces the levels or effects of mavacamten by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 15. Nafcillin decreases the levels or effects of naloxegol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is not recommended. 16. Nafcillin reduces the levels or effects of ombitasvir/paritaprevir/ritonavir and dasabuvir (DSC) by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated, as strong CYP3A4 inducers may reduce paritaprevir and ritonavir levels, decreasing the efficacy of Viekira Pak. 17. Nafcillin decreases the levels or effects of pacritinib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 18. Nafcillin reduces the levels of panobinostat by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated, as strong CYP3A4 inducers can reduce panobinostat levels by approximately 70%, leading to treatment failure. 19. Nafcillin decreases the levels or effects of regorafenib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated, as strong CYP3A4 inducers decrease regorafenib levels and increase exposure to its active metabolite M-5. 20. Nafcillin reduces the levels or effects of roflumilast by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is not recommended, as strong CYP3A4 inducers decrease systemic exposure to roflumilast, potentially reducing therapeutic effectiveness. 21. Nafcillin decreases the levels of vandetanib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated, as potent CYP3A4 inducers reduce vandetanib exposure by up to 40%. 22. Nafcillin reduces the levels or effects of abemaciclib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug, as strong CYP3A4 inducers reduce plasma concentrations of abemaciclib and its metabolites. 23. Nafcillin decreases the levels or effects of alpelisib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 24. Nafcillin reduces the levels or effects of apremilast by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug, as strong CYP3A4 inducers significantly decrease systemic exposure to apremilast, potentially reducing efficacy. 25. Nafcillin decreases the levels or effects of avapritinib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 26. Nafcillin reduces the levels of axitinib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. Select concomitant medications with no or minimal CYP3A4 induction potential. 27. Nafcillin decreases the effects of the BCG vaccine live by pharmacodynamic antagonism. Co-administration is contraindicated. Wait until antibiotic treatment is complete before administering live bacterial vaccines. 28. Nafcillin reduces the levels or effects of bedaquiline by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug, as strong CYP3A4 inducers may decrease therapeutic effects. 29. Nafcillin decreases the levels of bosutinib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug, as strong CYP3A4 inducers reduce bosutinib plasma concentration by approximately 85%. 30. Nafcillin reduces the levels or effects of brigatinib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug, as strong CYP3A4 inducers may decrease brigatinib efficacy. 31. Nafcillin decreases the levels or effects of cabozantinib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. If a strong CYP3A4 inducer is required, increase the cabozantinib dose by 40 mg/day (Cometriq) or 20 mg/day (Cabometyx). Resume the previous dose 2-3 days after discontinuing the inducer. 32. Nafcillin reduces the levels or effects of calcitriol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 33. Nafcillin decreases the levels or effects of capivasertib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug, as strong or moderate CYP3A4 inducers decrease capivasertib exposure, potentially reducing efficacy. 34. Nafcillin reduces the levels or effects of capmatinib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 35. Nafcillin decreases the levels of ceritinib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 36. Nafcillin reduces the effects of the cholera vaccine by pharmacodynamic antagonism. Avoid co-administration with systemic antibiotics, as these agents may be active against the vaccine strain. Do not administer the cholera vaccine to patients who have received oral or parenteral antibiotics within 14 days prior to vaccination. 37. Nafcillin decreases the levels or effects of cobicistat by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 38. Nafcillin reduces the levels or effects of copanlisib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 39. Nafcillin decreases the levels or effects of daridorexant by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 40. Nafcillin reduces the levels or effects of deflazacort by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. Avoid co-administration with moderate or strong CYP3A4 inducers. 41. Demeclocycline decreases the effects of nafcillin by pharmacodynamic antagonism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug, as bacteriostatic antibiotics may interfere with the bactericidal actions of penicillins. 42. Doxycycline decreases the effects of nafcillin by pharmacodynamic antagonism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug, as bacteriostatic antibiotics may interfere with the bactericidal actions of penicillins. 43. Nafcillin reduces the levels or effects of dronedarone by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 44. Nafcillin decreases the levels or effects of duvelisib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug, as strong CYP3A4 inducers decrease duvelisib area under the curve (AUC), potentially reducing efficacy. 45. Nafcillin reduces the levels or effects of elacestrant by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 46. Nafcillin decreases the levels or effects of elbasvir/grazoprevir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug, as moderate CYP3A4 inducers may reduce therapeutic effects. 47. Nafcillin reduces the levels or effects of eliglustat by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug, as strong CYP3A4 inducers significantly decrease eliglustat exposure. 48. Nafcillin decreases the levels or effects of elvitegravir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug, as CYP3A4 inducers may decrease plasma concentrations of elvitegravir and/or a concomitantly administered protease inhibitor, leading to loss of therapeutic effect and potential resistance. 49. Nafcillin reduces the levels or effects of encorafenib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 50. Nafcillin decreases the levels or effects of entrectinib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 51. Nafcillin reduces the levels or effects of erdafitinib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 52. Nafcillin decreases the levels or effects of erythromycin ethylsuccinate by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 53. Nafcillin reduces the levels or effects of erythromycin lactobionate by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 54. Nafcillin decreases the levels or effects of erythromycin stearate by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 55. Nafcillin reduces the levels or effects of everolimus by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 56. Nafcillin decreases the levels or effects of fedratinib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. The effect of co-administering a strong CYP3A4 inducer with fedratinib has not been studied. 57. Nafcillin increases the levels or effects of fexinidazole by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. Fexinidazole's active metabolites, fexinidazole sulfoxide (M1) and fexinidazole sulfone (M2), are associated with increased QT prolongation risks. 58. Nafcillin reduces the levels or effects of finerenone by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 59. Nafcillin decreases the levels or effects of fostamatinib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 60. Nafcillin reduces the levels or effects of fruquintinib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. If co-administration with moderate CYP3A4 inducers is unavoidable, continue fruquintinib at the recommended dosage. 61. Nafcillin decreases the levels or effects of ganaxolone by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. If co-administration is unavoidable, consider increasing the ganaxolone dose, but do not exceed the maximum daily dose for weight. 62. Nafcillin reduces the levels or effects of glasdegib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 63. Nafcillin decreases the levels of ibrutinib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug, as strong CYP3A4 inducers decrease ibrutinib plasma concentrations by approximately 10-fold. 64. Nafcillin reduces the levels or effects of idelalisib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug, as strong CYP3A4 inducers significantly decrease idelalisib systemic exposure. 65. Nafcillin decreases the levels or effects of infigratinib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug.
